text.title: C4 Drift Detection from IaC — Failure Modes
text.summary: 6 known failure modes of C4-versus-IaC drift detection. Each carries a detector (what to look for) and a repair (the corrective action).

failure-mode.description: Source, not state: the comparison reads HCL or the Pulumi program, so an unapplied or half-applied branch reports "no drift" while production differs from both.
failure-mode.detector: Comparison script parses `.tf`, `.ts` or template files; report carries no state serial, stack export version or stack id; a resource visible in the console is absent from the report.
failure-mode.repair: Switch the input to `terraform show -json`, `pulumi stack export` or `DescribeStackResources`; record the state identity in every report; add `terraform plan -refresh-only` to the schedule to catch out-of-band changes.

failure-mode.description: Picture as model: the "canonical" C4 is a PNG or draw.io file, so there are no element ids to difference and the report is a human's impression.
failure-mode.detector: No Structurizr DSL, LikeC4 or model JSON/YAML in version control; findings lack C4 element ids; report content varies with who ran it.
failure-mode.repair: Transcribe the diagram into a machine-readable model with stable ids once, render the pictures from it, and point the comparison at the model.

failure-mode.description: Silent residue: resource types the mapping table does not know are skipped, so a new managed database or queue never appears as `added`.
failure-mode.detector: Report has no `unmapped` section; count of state resources minus allowlisted minus mapped minus unmapped does not reconcile to zero.
failure-mode.repair: Emit every unmapped type with its count, reconcile the totals in the report header, and extend the mapping table in the same review.

failure-mode.description: Component level from state: the report claims component-level findings, producing a "removed" line for every component inside every deployable.
failure-mode.detector: Findings reference C4 components; hundreds of `removed` findings whose element ids sit inside a single container.
failure-mode.repair: State the compared level as Container in the report header, restrict the comparison to container and context elements, and document that component drift needs a code-level source.

failure-mode.description: Noise or hidden skips: either 400 findings of log groups and IAM roles get the report closed unread, or the script hard-codes skips and the one resource that mattered vanishes without a trace.
failure-mode.detector: First report has findings dominated by plumbing types; or comparison code contains type-based `continue` statements not present in the allowlist file; suppressed counts are not printed.
failure-mode.repair: Move every suppression into the version-controlled allowlist, print the suppressed count per entry, and remove skips from code.

failure-mode.description: Permanent drift: findings are acknowledged as "known" and carried forward for months, and the diagram stops being trusted.
failure-mode.detector: Same finding ids present across three or more consecutive reports; `accepted` entries with no expiry; no model commits linked from findings.
failure-mode.repair: Require every finding to close by model commit, IaC change or an accepted entry with a named reason and expiry inside one cadence; escalate two-report-old findings in the header.
